title: Volnewmer versus Thermage FLX, Ann Dermatol 2025;37:397–407; PMID41331720; DOI10.5021/ad.25.166
keyRecord: 22 Asian women; randomized split-face; one session; eight weeks; imaging and three blinded raters. Pain at 300 shots: 4.545±1.327 versus 8.386±1.174/10. Similar lifting/elasticity; some secondary endpoints favored Volnewmer; no significant persistent adverse event. No funding or conflicts declared.
limitations: Small, short study. An explicit clinical non-inferiority margin and margin-based CI analysis were not identified in the inspected methods; paired nonsignificance does not prove equivalence. Ex-vivo collagen was not participant biopsy or an identical two-device comparison.
rights: CC BY-NC4.0; unchanged NCBI OA transcription, attribution required; noncommercial research.

title: YOUMAGIC versus Thermage CPT RCT; PMID41758257; DOI10.1007/s10103-026-04841-4
keyRecord: 230 enrolled, 212 analyzed (107/105); six months; assessor-blinded; non-inferiority margin −10 percentage points; day-90 GAIS response 100%/98.10%; no serious adverse events. Manufacturer provided the device; registration retrospective.
limitations: CPT comparator, not FLX. No human collagen assay, predominantly female cohort, active comparator without sham.
rights: CC BY-NC-ND4.0 unchanged publisher PDF; existing R19 reused.

title: XERF prospective multicenter study; PMID41930066; PMC13040610; DOI10.7759/cureus.104546
keyRecord: 39 completers at four sites; two sessions; 30/90 days after final treatment; GAIS by treating principal investigators. Manufacturer equipment, consumables and grant; no persistent adverse events.
limitations: No control or blinded independent assessment or collagen biopsy. No human Thermage comparison; short follow-up. Responder percentages are not a cross-device efficacy ranking.
rights: CC BY4.0 OA transcription, attribution required.

title: XERF retrospective single-session study; PMID42611100; PMC13486139
keyRecord: 16 women; one session; formal three-month follow-up; 15 in periorbital analysis; 3D imaging/FACE-Q; transient events. Lead author is a manufacturer trainer; manufacturer assisted IRB submission and statistics. No external funding claimed.
limitations: No control or Thermage comparison. Volume surrogate does not validate anatomical repositioning. One illustrative six-month case was excluded from formal analysis. BioC endpoint unavailable; live PMC full text inspected.
rights: Bibliographic/support note only; no publisher full text redistributed.

title: Shin et al., Oligio aged faces; Cosmetics2024;11:71; DOI10.3390/cosmetics11030071
keyRecord: 20 women; one session; 24 weeks; three blinded photographic raters; firmness improved. Automated fine-wrinkle, pore and skin-tone changes were not significant. Mean pain 0.4/10 in results, despite no-pain abstract. No external funding or conflicts declared.
limitations: Uncontrolled; no Thermage comparison or collagen biopsy. Does not establish transfer to Oligio X/Kiss revisions. MDPI webpage returned 429; publisher PDF asset was live.

title: FDA XERF K251327, cleared2025-08-11
keyRecord: Monopolar 2/6.78 MHz; maximum 300/400 W respectively; FLX predicate. Intended use: electrocoagulation/hemostasis. Ex-vivo 3-mm temperature-time comparison; explicitly no clinical tests submitted.
limitations: Regulatory/ex-vivo bridge does not establish human wrinkle equivalence, cosmetic superiority, precise SMAS effect or universal fat preservation.
rights: Public regulator filing; initial request blocked, useragent retry livePDF.

title: FDA Volnewmer K240248, cleared2024-04-29
keyRecord: Monopolar 6.78 MHz, 115 W maximum; water cooling; Thermage FLX predicate. Intended use: dermatologic electrocoagulation/hemostasis. Bench/in-vivo thermal testing.
limitations: Narrow intended-use wording; does not transfer all predicate wrinkle/eyelid indications or establish equal human efficacy.
rights: Public regulator filing; initial request blocked, useragent retry livePDF.

title: FDA Thermage FLX K170758, cleared2017-09-22
keyRecord: RF-only indications: electrocoagulation/hemostasis and noninvasive wrinkles, including upper/lower eyelids. RF-plus-vibration wording separately lists periorbital wrinkles/rhytids, wrinkles/rhytids and temporary cellulite appearance improvement.
limitations: Indication wording does not guarantee results, a universal dose or equal competitor labeling. Database also checked: https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/scripts/cdrh/cfdocs/cfpmn/pmn.cfm?ID=K170758

title: FDA Oligio K221989, cleared2022-10-13
keyRecord: Monopolar 6.78 MHz, 145 W maximum; cooling gas; FLX predicate. Intended use: dermatologic/general surgical electrocoagulation/hemostasis.
limitations: Not a human Thermage comparison. Does not establish revised Oligio X/Kiss equivalence.
rights: Public regulator filing; initial request blocked, useragent retry livePDF.

title: Oku Density Mono-Bi CrossLIFT; PMID41090512; PMC12522179; DOI10.1111/jocd.70504
keyRecord: 16 adults aged 36–59, Fitzpatrick II–IV; one session; 24 weeks; 3D imaging. Tightening: abstract 0.82±0.36 mm, body SD 0.34. GAIS improved in 15/16; pain 1.4±0.6/5; no severe adverse events. Single author declared no conflicts.
limitations: Uncontrolled; protocol-specific imaging does not quantify collagen or fat loss. No Thermage comparison.
rights: CC BY4.0 OA transcription with attribution.

title: Volnewmer versus Thermage CPT registry NCT06657365
keyRecord: Official API snapshot October 2, 2026: COMPLETED; completion July 3, 2025; last update posted May 4, 2026; no resultsSection. API: https://clinicaltrials.gov/api/v2/studies/NCT06657365
limitations: Registration/status is not an outcome. Different record from the published 2025 FLX split-face trial.

title: FDA RF microneedling safety communication,2025-10-15
keyRecord: FDA reports burns, scarring, fat loss, disfigurement and nerve damage with certain RF microneedling uses; medical procedure; not for home use; seek a licensed trained provider. Evaluation ongoing. Existing R21 reused.
limitations: Microneedling-specific communication; does not establish all noninvasive RF risks, incidence or a causal device ranking.
